recent_decisions.decision: NEXT, dispatched: ONE structural fix in tree_mesh.rs unlocks canopies for the two remaining forms. recent_decisions.decision: FIVE-TRACK ENVIRONMENT AUDIT LANDED (21 agents, adversarially verified, plan at %TEMP%/plan.md). HEADLINE: THE RENDERER HAS NO INDIRECT LIGHT. ambient = albedo * vec3(0.005) at 90-fragment-main.wgsl:1656 is the only ambient in the engine; a grep for texture_cube|env_map|prefilter|brdf_lut|irradiance|spherical_harmon returns COMMENTS ONLY. The one thing acting as indirect is a WORLD-FIXED directional fill (lib.rs:12099) that swings below the local horizon over a day on a rotating true-scale planet and also paints a meaningless specular lobe. Everything else in the list is downstream of that. TIER S: S1 sky irradiance from the ALREADY-BOUND sky-view LUT (binding 13, zero new bindings - the v0.1029 incident class stays closed) with max(sky, 0.005 floor) because the celestial pass alone writes those pads and interiors/space would otherwise go to EXACTLY ZERO; S2 shadow strength 0.6->1.0 (a fully occluded fragment keeps 40% of full sun IN THE SUN WARM COLOUR; measured shadow/lit 0.412-0.432 vs a physical 0.10-0.20 AND BLUE); S3a AO off albedo onto the indirect term; S4 fog phase function (toward-sun and away are currently BIT-IDENTICAL; the engine already owns cloud_phase measured 9.12 forward:back and uses it nowhere in fog).
recent_decisions.why: One systemic cause behind grass-too-dark, cut-out silhouettes, flat-white fog and shadows that read wrong.

recent_decisions.decision: PROCESS WIN worth keeping: the grass writer REFUTED ITS OWN leading hypothesis. It built the per-cell-ladder fix for the rings, made the gate fail on purpose against un-jittered code, and the gate DID NOT FIRE (CV 1.08 vs 1.07) - so it reverted a change that would have moved every tiller in the world for no measurable gain. Then it found its own statistic was blunt, re-pointed it at within-cell threshold gaps, and re-ran a forced ladder: 1.00 forced vs 0.03 shipped, 33x separation. THE REAL RING CANDIDATE, found and deliberately NOT silently fixed: the density ramp is C0 but not C1 - slope jumps at 6m, 12m, 22m, and a first-derivative discontinuity in a density field is a Mach band, i.e. three faint rings at exactly those radii moving with the player. Every C1 profile through the same anchors costs +25-49% instances, so the cheap fix is a parabolic fillet at each knee (mass-neutral to 2nd order, still closed-form invertible for grass_appear_distance). NEXT INCREMENT in the grass lane.

recent_decisions.decision: v0.1107 root causes, all MEASURED, from a 13-agent adversarial workflow. (1) TREE SELECTION WAS NOT SELECTING: near_trees.rs returned early on max_n HUNDREDS OF LINES ABOVE its nearest-first sort; the cap bound in all 3587 logged frames, so the sort never ran in a shipped frame and the 256-model budget went in raw cell-walk order (entry #256 at 162m while a 30m tree got nothing) = billboards phasing out + open-field-then-forest. Now harvest whole disc, sort by TRUE 3D distance, truncate after. NEW GATE asserts a capped harvest is a PREFIX of the sorted one - fails on the restored bug at TREE 0. (2) SHADOWS WITHOUT TREES: both shadow pipelines were fragment: None (pipeline.rs:564,:709 - the only two in the file), so a 21m card that is 15-25% opaque cast a solid board ~36m downsun. New fs_shadow reproduces FOUR discards; the fourth (LOD crossfade dither) is the only patch-granular movement-coupled one and is the exact match for as-I-move-the-empty-chunk-changes. Classic pipeline SPLITS so opaque geometry keeps depth-only. Cost 30 -> 23.8 fps; two discards INERT until per-material albedo is bound into the shadow pass (filed). (3) TREELESS RING: hide derived from covered_r2 (what actually drew) clamped to tree_dist; was 45.2% of frames with hide > tree_dist, worst 172m vs 120m reach. Probe after: covered=90m hide=82m. (4) TRIANGLE LEAVES: fir/pine were 7508 faces = 91% of the tree and 100% of its silhouette; cluster blocks make them vanish by construction AND cost 31% LESS (5732 vs 8260).
recent_decisions.why: Four of the operator seven reports, one root cause each.

recent_decisions.decision: OPERATOR: finish the called-out items. FOUR LANES DISPATCHED, disjoint files. (A) CONTINUOUS BIOME GATE - veg_biome_ok at planet_chunks.rs:456-458 is a BINARY threshold on two imagery colour ratios sampled on a ~1m bilinear lattice, and it is the ONLY mechanism in the data that can make PATCHES: measured 0 tillers at one parked pose vs 5930 at the next vs 31635-32958 in three other rigs, same vantage/exe/density. Becomes a 0..1 smoothstep weight multiplied into density at both the grass and tree sites. Also asked to check whether it has the SAME raw-vs-graded colour-space bug the ground classifier had. (B) SHADOW ALBEDO BINDING - two of fs_shadow four discards (type-19 photoscan, type-21 card) are INERT because the shadow pass binds one group-3 whose binding 0 is a 1x1 WHITE fallback; needs a second per-material bind group with dummy_depth at binding 6 (the real shadow_map_view is the pass own depth attachment = exclusive-usage conflict). Same lane narrows the caster selector so opaque bark stops paying for a fragment stage that discards nothing. renderer/mod.rs is at 3883/3883 so it must extract. (C) OCEAN WHITE-OUT + 15fps FOREST - read-only diagnosis, the only agent permitted to boot tonight. (D) THE PLAYER IS ON A 2.5m STILT: EYE_HEIGHT_M 1.7 + LOD_CLEARANCE_M 2.5 rests the eye 4.2m above ground, looking at a 0.24-0.52m sward - a first-class candidate for grass-never-gets-further-away, and it inflates every grazing-cover figure ~2.5x. The fix is to rest on the DRAWN surface (DrawnPatchSurface), which is exactly what grass did in v0.1091 and trees in v0.1097 for the same reason; the clearance is a band-aid over the drawn-vs-fine mismatch.

recent_decisions.decision: v0.1108 SHIPPED, four lanes. (1) THE PLAYER WAS ON A 2.5m STILT: EYE_HEIGHT_M 1.7 + LOD_CLEARANCE_M 2.5 rested the eye 4.2m above a 0.24-0.52m sward - a first-class cause of grass-never-gets-further-away, and it inflated every ground-cover figure ~2.5x. Measured before deleting: worst upward drawn-vs-fine bulge is +0.462m across 5 sites x 3 depths x 441 samples on the REAL earth.ron relief (the test fixture would have inflated it 3.5x), so 2.5 was 5x oversized. Fixed the way grass (v0.1091) and trees (v0.1097) were: STAND ON DrawnPatchSurface. Clearance now 0.05m; 2.5 survives only as the unknown-depth fallback. Gate measures against the REAL built patch mesh via Moller-Trumbore, never against the sampler itself. RED 4.15-4.28m -> GREEN 1.750m at all 15 site/depth combos. (2) BIOME EDGES: veg_biome_ok was a binary threshold on imagery ratios sampled on a 9.78 KM texel - a whole grass disc inside one bilinear cell - measured 32,817 tillers -> ZERO in one 380m step, 13,966 adjacent land pairs straddling the cut. Now a 0..1 smoothstep weight at the grass, near-tree AND far-sheet sites; ecotone ~5km. Ramps calibrated from shipped imagery: r/g is the discriminator (71.6pt separation), g/b is NOT a vegetation discriminator at all (keeps 98% vegetated AND 87% barren at every cut) - its job is water/ice rejection. Mean weight 84.2% vs the old bool 84.4%, which is why no LAI gate moved.

recent_decisions.decision: v0.1108 cont. (3) FOLIAGE CUTOUT SHADOWS NOW ACTUALLY LIVE: the shadow pass bound ONE group-3 whose binding 0 is a 1x1 OPAQUE WHITE texture, so the two foliage discards sampled alpha 1, could never fire, AND cost a fragment stage + texture fetch on up to 1536 objects/frame. Each material now carries a shadow-safe bind group (same 16 entries, dummy depth at binding 6 - the real shadow map is the pass own depth attachment, RESOURCE+DEPTH_STENCIL_WRITE is exclusive). Both groups built by ONE closure differing only in that view, so identical-except-binding-6 is a property of the code shape. Selector was wrong in BOTH directions (opaque bark paying; untextured type-12 patches NOT paying despite drawing sprite cards) and now derives from the shader own type bands, pinned by a test that PARSES THOSE BANDS OUT OF THE ASSEMBLED SHADER. LATENT BUG found: patch_pipeline_layout differs at group 1 so set_pipeline(patch_shadow_pipeline) invalidates groups 1..3 per the WebGPU compat rule; the colour pass re-set group 3, the shadow pass did not. (4) SKY/SEA FOG PARITY: the same fog was integrated as a SLANT path for the sea (cap/sin, 2286m at the horizon) and a FLAT 80m layer for the sky - measured 99.7% fog on water, 18.8% sky, 0% clouds, which is why the water read as broken when it was the only surface telling the truth. recent_decisions.decision: CORRECTIONS TO MY OWN CLAIMS, both measured by an independent critic. (a) I told the operator the shadow fragment stage cost 30 -> 23.8 fps. REFUTED: their display is 119Hz with vsync ON, so every reading quantises to 119/n - 23.8 is 119/5, 30 is 119/4, 15 is 119/8. Those are vsync interval counts, not work measurements. Timestamp-queried gpu.shadow across three existing dumps is 1.38/2.81/2.95 ms for the WHOLE pass, so a fragment stage cannot have cost 8ms. NEVER quote an fps delta from a vsync-capped run again. (b) The critic also found the scene swings 44.3 -> 101.1 ms with the camera PARKED and byte-identical content for 35 minutes - a 2.3x swing with nothing changing - and refuted god rays and grass CPU as the cause. CANNOT-DETERMINE without a vsync-off controlled run; the rig own config has vsync:true, which is why the vantage note quotes a 33.3ms ceiling. STILL OPEN: grass ramp reshape (item 7, costs 2.55x and needs distance-bucketed blade LOD FIRST); tree identity + sparse delta store for felling (item 12, 10 bytes on NearTree); near-camera cluster cards reading as flat sheets; fog_density slider saturates above ~1.4 (lib.rs one-liner, deferred while lib.rs was contended).

recent_decisions.decision: The leaf tufts were geometrically cubes, and the gate that could see it had to be built before the fix could be judged.
recent_decisions.why: The operator said "the bunches of leaves look a little weird, kind of like they are cubes." The first instrument grouped cards by PROXIMITY and reported 0.31 against a 0.30 threshold - nearly a false pass. Grouping exactly (one emit_sleeve call is one sleeve) showed the truth: conifer tufts were 100% parallel card pairs, broadleaf tufts 67% perpendicular plus 33% parallel. The golden-angle azimuth fix alone left 33% still near-perpendicular because the normals stayed on one circle; the tilt half is what cleared it, and stratifying those tilts in solid-angle bands (right for POINTS) measured WORSE than no tilt at all, because a sleeve is a set of PLANES. Line packing, not point scattering.

recent_decisions.decision: The canopy parity gate records the level PER SPECIES rather than widening one band.
recent_decisions.why: Broadleaf crowns land on the isotropic leaf-angle kernel almost exactly (0.94-1.05). Fir and pine sit 22% under it at every sun angle, and that is real: a fir carries flat sprays along a branch and the spherify blend pushes its normals horizontal. A single band loose enough to admit 1.30 would stop noticing a broadleaf that broke. The ratio is near-constant in sun angle for every species, so the kernel SHAPE is right and only the LEVEL is species-dependent - driving those to 1.00 wants a per-species scalar baked into the billboard atlas, which is named as the follow-up rather than hidden.

recent_decisions.decision: The float-up/fall-down bug was frame rate, not pitch.
recent_decisions.why: Looking at vegetation costs frames; the frame-lock sampled terrain at a point that lagged the player by one frame of planetary spin, which is 33,360 m/s of ground slip on the 20-minute day. So the altitude reading was proportional to frame time, crossed the drawn-ground gate, and flipped stand height by 2.45 m. v0.1108 patched the same defect at the symptom. Lesson: when a symptom correlates with where the camera points, ask what the camera pointing CHANGES (here: load) before assuming the direction itself is the input.

recent_decisions.decision: Forest density became an explicit argument and the process-global atomic was DELETED, not left as a bridge.
recent_decisions.why: Two vegetation streams (card bake, model harvest) each read the global for themselves. Measured: 32.51% of northern cells disagreed at density 0.6294 because the bake rounded twice and the harvest once, and count is the survival-gate threshold rather than a loop bound. Even the shipped 0.6 default split one cell row at 21.2N. Separately a slider drag left models up to 12 m of walking behind the cards, and a card with no model discards in the colour pass while still casting shade. Invariant adopted: every card that can be on screen has a model in it, which works because the enumeration is monotone in density. Callers wanting ground geometry take a FIXED AGNOSTIC_TREE_DENSITY pinned to the shipped default by a test - leaving one global reader behind would leave the door open.

recent_decisions.decision: The conifer card over-brightness was the odd component of the shading normals, not anisotropic foliage.
recent_decisions.why: I told the operator it was real fir anisotropy. Wrong. A crown area-weighted mean shading normal is nonzero (fir 0.1221 down to momiji 0.0217) and that ordering matches the brightness ordering exactly; it survives max(N.L,0) because a card gives both windings the same normal. Cancelled at source by solving for the correction that drives the mean to zero. An adversarial reviewer REFUTED the geometric just-so story offered for why the mean points down while reproducing the arithmetic, so the comments now say the first moment is measured, not derived. Recording a limitation in a gate was right while it was a limitation and wrong to keep once it was fixable.

recent_decisions.decision: A three-lane merge was committed under a one-lane message and immediately reset.
recent_decisions.why: git apply --3way STAGES what it applies. After applying three worktree patches, adding three files by name added to an index that already held all nine, so the commit swept every lane under a message describing one - the exact failure the shared-checkout rule exists to prevent. Caught by reading git show --stat AFTER committing, which is too late. Rule: after any git apply, run git reset before staging, and check git diff --cached --stat BEFORE the commit.

recent_decisions.decision: View-frustum culling of near trees is the largest verified unclaimed win: 62% of the draw budget is spent behind the camera.
recent_decisions.why: Measured at the operator settings two independent ways (engine harness plus first-principles geometry, agreeing within 1.5pp). Respending that budget on visible trees moves the model reach 181 m to 300 m, 2.9x the area for the same draw count. NOT a one-line change: three coverage rules were tested and only one works (visible trees feed ModelCoverage AND the hide radius is clamped by the harvest edge). Naive skip gives a 190 m bare ring in FRONT of the player; naive uncovered gives a 4.7 m radius so nothing ever hides. The cull bound must enclose the CARD (acacia is 1.365x height), not the trunk. The shadow pass must stay unculled: near-tree models are the only off-screen casters, and 44-61% of culled trees cast into view at an 8 degree sun. The v0.995 reason for view-independence died with the v0.1110.2 ModelCoverage rewrite.

recent_decisions.decision: The 103 ms forest frame is still UNEXPLAINED and no perf fix should be ranked until it is.
recent_decisions.why: An agent concluded CPU-submission-bound; the reviewer took it apart, because that rested on zero measurement of the actual frame. Named CPU is ~35 ms of 103. The only GPU data says the pass CONTAINING grass is 68-91% of GPU time, and it just received 10-30x more geometry (245,605 tufts, ~32M tris) - so the evidence points opposite to the conclusion. Also unexplained and already on record: the same scene, camera PARKED on byte-identical content, swinging 44.3 to 101.1 ms over 35 minutes. Do not rank grass culling vs blade LOD vs draw batching until the per-pass breakdown is real.

recent_decisions.decision: Sliders snap to their displayed precision; the snap is drag-only.
recent_decisions.why: The operator asked for it after seeing 9.579/0.6294 in the divergence report - values the slider produced and then hid behind a rounded label. Snapping in the one drag funnel (custom_slider_with_width) makes stored == shown and the input space finite, so agreement gates can enumerate rather than sample. Typed values stay exact: typing is intent, dragging is aiming. Existing configs untouched until the next drag. The gate duplicates the handler arithmetic instead of driving a headless Ui - a stated coupling, cheap at 3% budget; the assertion message tells whoever changes the display rule to change the step in the same commit.
